title: Father, Supply My Every Need
description: Father, Supply My Every Need in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 501, “The Bread of Life”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther, sup-ply my ev-ery need; Sus-tain the life Thy-self hast given; Oh! grant the nev-er fail-ing bread, The man-na that comes down from heaven!

lines: Sustain the life Thyself hast given;
The manna that comes down from heaven!
Nor ever let me hunger more!

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
